dedupe_keys.name: liwo national flood and inundation map layers netherlands

description: LIWO, the Dutch national information system on water and floods, is a map viewer and set of map services from the Watermanagementcentrum Nederland at Rijkswaterstaat, built by Deltares and HKV, that gives professionals the flood layers they need to prepare for flooding and waterlogging in the Netherlands. Its layers come from the national flood information database (LDO), into which provinces, water boards and Rijkswaterstaat deliver breach scenarios. They include maximum flood depth for outer-dike areas and for breaches of primary and non-primary flood defences, individual breach scenarios with effect maps that can be combined online, EU Floods Directive maps, pluvial flooding from short intense rain, flood probabilities and flood risk now and at the 2050 and 2100 horizons, evacuation percentages, warning and water arrival times, flood duration and dry floors per building and neighbourhood. The viewer is open to all, layers are also served as WMS, content may be reused with attribution to LIWO and WMCN, and releases are periodic, the latest being 2025.1.6 in October 2025. Caveats: IPLO warns that reading the layers needs specialist knowledge from water managers, scenario resolution and dates differ by source holder, no open licence is named and bulk download was not confirmed. Simulation uses: flood exposure of assets and people behind dikes, evacuation and crisis planning, cascading impacts of dike breaches on other networks, and climate adaptation of spatial plans. Related record: the national primary flood defence data (data-netherlands-primary-flood-defences-nbpw) gives the dike trajectories and safety standards the breach scenarios refer to.
licence: Reuse of content allowed with attribution to LIWO, Watermanagementcentrum Nederland (copyright reserved by WMCN; no open licence named)
